intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes
experiences.description: Hit the world-class slopes of the Jungfrau region, covering Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren. With over 200km of marked runs suitable for all skill levels, families can enjoy beginner-friendly blue runs while more experienced skiers tackle challenging red and black descents. Ski school options are available for children aged 3 and up.

experiences.name: Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking in Zermatt
experiences.description: Explore the stunning snow-covered trails around Zermatt on a guided family snowshoeing tour. Trek through pristine alpine forests and open meadows with breathtaking views of the iconic Matterhorn. Guides provide all equipment and tailor the pace for families with children, making it an accessible and memorable winter adventure.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, stretching over 3km through scenic alpine terrain. Rent sleds at the top and race down the illuminated track as a family. Evening runs under the stars add a magical touch, and the nearby village offers warm Swiss hot chocolate and raclette to round off the adventure.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. Enjoy classic cheese fondue made with Gruyère and Emmental, paired with crusty bread, charcuterie, and local Valais wine for adults. Many chalets offer family-friendly menus and a rustic, authentic alpine atmosphere that kids love.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Excursion
experiences.description: Take the iconic cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, walk on the glacier, and enjoy panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The visitor center offers interactive exhibits about alpine science and history, making it both educational and awe-inspiring for the whole family.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel time from airport to Grindelwald-Wengen (approx. 2.5–3 hrs via train from Zurich Airport: Zurich HB → Interlaken Ost → Grindelwald). Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or regional Jungfrau Travel Pass at the airport to save on transport costs throughout the week.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Boutique Stay in Grindelwald-Wengen, check in and settle in. Take a leisurely orientation walk through Grindelwald village. Stroll along the main street (Dorfstrasse), admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face, and locate the ski rental shops to compare prices. Book ski equipment rental in advance at shops like Intersport or Alpin Sports for best budget rates.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the village further as the sun sets over the Alps. Visit the Grindelwald Tourist Office to collect free maps, trail guides, and check for any family discount passes or combo ski lift tickets for the week.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or sandwich at Zurich Airport before or after landing — budget CHF 8–12.
meals.lunch: Pick up a pretzel, wurst, or a packed sandwich from a Migros or Coop supermarket near Interlaken Ost train station during the transfer — budget CHF 6–10.
meals.dinner: Dine at Restaurant Pizzeria Alte Post in Grindelwald — a local favorite offering hearty Swiss and Italian dishes at reasonable prices. Try the cheese fondue or pasta. Budget CHF 18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a Jungfrau Travel Pass (3-day or 5-day) at the start — it covers trains, buses, and select ski lifts in the region and offers significant savings for families. Migros and Coop supermarkets are your best friends for budget snacks and groceries throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: First full ski day! Head to the Grindelwald-First ski area, one of the most family-friendly ski zones in the Jungfrau Region. Beginners and children can take lessons at the First ski school (book in advance for group lessons to save money). Intermediate and experienced skiers can enjoy the 45 km of groomed pistes. Lifts open around 08:30 — arrive early to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the First slopes. After lunch, try the First Flyer zip line or the First Cliff Walk (free to walk, no extra charge beyond lift ticket) for a thrilling non-ski activity the whole family can enjoy. Children under 9 ski free with a paying adult on Jungfrau ski passes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by 16:30. Warm up with a hot chocolate at a local café. Visit the Grindelwald Sports Centre (Sportzentrum) for ice skating — a fun, affordable family evening activity (skate rental + entry approx. CHF 10–15 per person).

meals.breakfast: Prepare breakfast at the boutique stay using groceries from Coop/Migros (bread, cheese, yogurt, fruit) — budget CHF 5–8 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and thermoses of hot soup or cocoa to eat on the mountain — saves CHF 20–30 per person compared to mountain restaurants. Alternatively, use the self-service section at Bergrestaurant First (budget CHF 12–16).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or raclette dinner at the accommodation if kitchen facilities are available, or dine at Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald for affordable Swiss comfort food — budget CHF 15–22 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski equipment for the full week upfront — daily rental is more expensive. Helmets are strongly recommended for children and are often included in family rental packages. Check weather forecasts each morning at grindelwald.ch or the Jungfrau webcams.

day_by_day.morning: Take the scenic Wengernalpbahn (WAB) cogwheel train from Grindelwald Grund up to Kleine Scheidegg (covered by Jungfrau Travel Pass). This is a spectacular family experience with breathtaking views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. At Kleine Scheidegg, enjoy beginner-friendly ski slopes or take a snowshoe walk along marked trails (snowshoe rental approx. CHF 12/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: From Kleine Scheidegg, ski or sled down the Lauberhorn area toward Wengen — one of the most famous ski runs in the world (site of the annual Lauberhorn World Cup race). Families can ride the train back down from Wengen to Grindelwald Grund if needed. Alternatively, take a guided family sledding run on designated sled tracks — sled rental is budget-friendly at CHF 8–12.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the free Grindelwald village Christmas/winter market stalls (if running in February) or browse local craft shops. Enjoy a quiet evening walk under the stars with views of the illuminated Eiger.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at accommodation — oatmeal, bread, eggs, and Swiss cheese — budget CHF 4–7 per person.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Bahnhof Buffet at Kleine Scheidegg — affordable train station café with hot soups, sandwiches, and drinks. Budget CHF 12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Try Restaurant Café 3692 in Grindelwald for Swiss rösti, raclette, and local specialties at mid-range prices. Budget CHF 18–26 per person. Share dishes as a family to reduce costs.

day_by_day.notes: The WAB cogwheel train to Kleine Scheidegg is a highlight for kids and adults alike — sit on the right side going up for the best Eiger views. Wengen is a car-free village, making it very safe and peaceful for families.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mürren — a stunning car-free mountain village. Take the train from Grindelwald to Lauterbrunnen, then the cable car up to Grütschalp, and the mountain railway to Mürren (all covered by Jungfrau Travel Pass). Ski the Schilthorn area — famous for the James Bond film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service.' The Mürren-Schilthorn ski area has 55 km of varied pistes suitable for all levels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Piz Gloria revolving restaurant at the top of Schilthorn (2,970 m) — entry is free if you purchase a meal or drink (budget CHF 15–20). Enjoy 360° panoramic views of over 200 Alpine peaks including the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Kids love the James Bond exhibition. Ski back down to Mürren in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald via Lauterbrunnen by 17:30. Relax at the accommodation. Optional: visit a local fondue restaurant for a classic Swiss family dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at accommodation — budget CHF 4–7 per person.
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch (sandwiches, energy bars, fruit) to eat on the mountain or at Mürren village. Alternatively, grab a quick bite at the Schilthorn summit café — budget CHF 12–18.
meals.dinner: Dine at Restaurant Firestarter in Grindelwald — known for affordable burgers, wraps, and family-friendly menu. Budget CHF 14–20 per person. Or self-cater at accommodation with fondue kits available from Coop supermarket (CHF 8–10 for a kit serving 2).

day_by_day.notes: The journey to Mürren is an adventure in itself — the Lauterbrunnen valley with its 72 waterfalls is stunning even in winter. Mürren is one of the most beautiful Alpine villages in Switzerland and is entirely traffic-free, making it ideal for families with young children.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated family ski day at Männlichen — accessible by cable car from Grindelwald Grund (included in Jungfrau ski pass). Männlichen offers wide, gentle slopes ideal for beginners and children, plus more challenging runs for experienced skiers. The Männlichen ski school offers affordable group lessons — book the 'Fun Ski' family package.
day_by_day.afternoon: After skiing, take the Royal Walk from Männlichen summit — a short, easy 30-minute signposted winter walk with spectacular views of the Grindelwald valley and surrounding peaks. This is free and suitable for all ages and fitness levels. Descend via cable car or ski back to Grindelwald Grund.
day_by_day.evening: Treat the family to a traditional Swiss cheese fondue or raclette dinner at a local restaurant — a must-do cultural experience. Pre-book to secure a table on a Friday evening.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared hearty breakfast before a full ski day — porridge, eggs, bread, and hot drinks — budget CHF 5–8 per person.
meals.lunch: Use the self-service restaurant at Männlichen mountain station — choose soup, bread, and a hot drink to keep costs down. Budget CHF 10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chalet Suisse in Grindelwald for authentic fondue and raclette in a cozy Alpine chalet setting. Budget CHF 20–28 per person. Kids' menus available.

day_by_day.notes: The Männlichen–Kleine Scheidegg ski run is one of the longest and most scenic beginner/intermediate runs in the Alps at over 7 km — a memorable experience for the whole family. Fridays can be busier with weekend crowds arriving, so hit the slopes early.

day_by_day.morning: Take a once-in-a-lifetime trip to Jungfraujoch — 'Top of Europe' at 3,454 m, the highest railway station in Europe. Book tickets in advance online for the best price (approx. CHF 145–175 per adult with Swiss Travel Pass discount; children under 16 receive significant discounts). Depart from Grindelwald Grund or Kleine Scheidegg by 08:00 to beat the crowds and enjoy clear morning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Jungfraujoch: visit the Ice Palace (carved entirely from glacier ice), the Sphinx Observatory viewing platform, and the Snow Fun Park where kids can try snow tubing, zip lines, and sledding (some activities included in ticket). Walk on the Aletsch Glacier — the longest glacier in the Alps. Return to Grindelwald by 14:00–15:00.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final full evening in Grindelwald. Browse the village shops for Swiss souvenirs (chocolate, cheese, Swiss Army knives). Enjoy a farewell dinner at a local restaurant. Pack bags for departure the next day.

meals.breakfast: Early self-prepared breakfast at accommodation before the Jungfraujoch departure — budget CHF 4–7 per person.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch — a self-service option that is more affordable than the sit-down restaurants at the summit. Budget CHF 18–25 per person (mountain prices are higher — budget accordingly). Alternatively, pack sandwiches to eat on the train or at the summit.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on the last full night — dine at Restaurant Mercado in Grindelwald for a varied international and Swiss menu in a warm atmosphere. Budget CHF 22–30 per person. Share starters and desserts to manage costs.

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch is the most expensive single activity of the trip but is an unmissable, bucket-list experience — especially magical for children. Dress in very warm layers (temperatures at the top can be -15°C to -20°C in February). The Jungfrau Travel Pass offers a discounted 'Good Morning Ticket' if you take the first train — check availability when booking. Saturday is the busiest day, so an early start is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Grindelwald. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast and check out of the accommodation. Take one last walk through the village for final photos of the Eiger. If time permits, visit the free Grindelwald Museum (Heimatmuseum) to learn about the region's Alpine history and culture — a low-cost, enriching activity for the family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the journey home. Take the train from Grindelwald to Interlaken Ost, then connect to Bern or Zurich for onward flights. The journey from Grindelwald to Zurich Airport takes approximately 2.5–3 hours — plan to arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Return any rented ski equipment before catching the train.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, mountain adventures, and Swiss Alpine culture with the family.

meals.breakfast: Final self-prepared or café breakfast in Grindelwald — try Café 3692 or the hotel breakfast if included. Budget CHF 8–15 per person.
meals.lunch: Grab a takeaway sandwich, pretzel, or salad from Coop or Migros at Interlaken Ost or Zurich main station during the transfer — budget CHF 8–12 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich Airport or on the flight home. Budget CHF 15–25 at airport restaurants, or pack snacks from the supermarket for the journey.

day_by_day.notes: Return ski rental equipment early on the final morning to avoid extra charges. Keep your Swiss Travel Pass or Jungfrau Travel Pass handy for the journey back to the airport — it covers most train connections. Use any remaining Swiss Francs to buy Swiss chocolate at the supermarket (Lindt, Toblerone, Läderach) — far cheaper than at the airport. Total estimated budget for 7 days per person (excluding flights and accommodation): CHF 600–900, including ski passes, equipment rental, meals, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Use morning for in-flight rest and preparation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and collect luggage (~45 min), then board the scenic Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) train from Zurich HB to Grindelwald via Interlaken Ost and Grindelwald terminal (~2.5 hrs). Arrive at your Boutique Stay in Grindelwald by approximately 16:30. Check in, unpack, and take a leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village to get your bearings — admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face glowing in the late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a cozy local restaurant in Grindelwald village for a relaxed welcome dinner. Explore the village's charming main street, pick up any forgotten essentials at a local shop, and return to the hotel for an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal or airport café snack at Zurich Airport before boarding the train.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Zurich HB train station — try a Migros or Coop to Go sandwich or a pretzel (budget-friendly, ~CHF 8–12).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte or similar mid-range Grindelwald eatery — enjoy a hearty Swiss Rösti with raclette cheese and a local Rugenbrau beer (~CHF 30–40 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or Jungfrau Travel Pass upon arrival at Zurich HB — it covers trains, buses, and many mountain railways, saving significant money over 7 days. Validate it immediately. Confirm ski rental reservations for Day 2 with the hotel concierge tonight.

day_by_day.morning: First full day on the slopes! Head to Grindelwald First ski area (accessible by gondola from the village, ~10 min walk from most hotels). Pick up pre-booked ski rentals at Grindelwald Sports or a slope-side rental shop. Spend the morning getting your ski legs on the blue and red runs of the Jungfrau Ski Region — Grindelwald First sector offers excellent groomed pistes ideal for warming up. Ski instructors available for children if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes — transition to the Kleine Scheidegg sector via the Männlichen gondola for more varied terrain. Enjoy panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau from the ridgeline runs. Families can enjoy the gentler Wengernalp slopes while more experienced skiers tackle the challenging Lauberhorn descent.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski equipment and head back to the hotel to freshen up. Walk into Grindelwald village for dinner at a traditional mountain restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique hotel (typically included — enjoy fresh bread, Swiss cheese, cold cuts, yogurt, and coffee).
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Bergrestaurant Grindelwald First — try the Älplermagronen (Alpine mac & cheese with applesauce) or a warming soup (~CHF 18–25 per person).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Mercado or Café 3692 in Grindelwald — hearty pasta, salads, and Swiss mains at mid-range prices (~CHF 28–38 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Jungfrau Ski Region lift passes can be purchased at the gondola base station or online in advance. A 1-day adult pass is approximately CHF 75–85; children under 9 ski free with a paying adult. Dress in warm layers — February temperatures on the slopes can drop to -10°C or lower with wind chill. Apply high-SPF sunscreen — UV exposure is intense at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the iconic Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Excursion — the highlight of the Jungfrau region. Walk to Grindelwald terminal and board the Eiger Express gondola to Eigergletscher, then connect to the historic cogwheel train up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters. Arrive at the highest railway station in Europe and explore the Sphinx Observatory, Ice Palace (carved entirely from glacier ice), and the vast Aletsch Glacier panorama. Allow 3–4 hours at the summit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the descent back to Grindelwald by early afternoon (~13:30–14:00 departure from Jungfraujoch). On the way down, stop at Kleine Scheidegg for a short scenic walk along the ridge with breathtaking Eiger views. Return to Grindelwald by 15:30. Rest at the hotel or explore Grindelwald's local shops and galleries — pick up Swiss chocolate or souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Treat the family to the Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience at a traditional mountain chalet restaurant. Gather around a bubbling pot of Gruyère and Emmental cheese fondue, dipping crusty bread cubes while warming up after a high-altitude day. A quintessential Swiss Alps memory.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — fuel up well before the high-altitude excursion. Drink extra water to prepare for altitude.
meals.lunch: Restaurant Crystal at Jungfraujoch (3,454m) — enjoy a bowl of hot soup or a light meal with the most spectacular dining view in Switzerland (~CHF 20–30 per person). Alternatively, bring snacks from the hotel to save costs.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner at Restaurant Adler or Chalet-Hotel Gletschergarten — cheese fondue set menu with salad and dessert (~CHF 40–55 per person including wine or soft drinks).

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch tickets well in advance — February is peak season and trains fill up quickly. Round-trip from Grindelwald costs approximately CHF 145–160 per adult (discounts with Swiss Travel Pass). Children under 16 receive significant discounts. Altitude sickness is possible at 3,454m — take it slow, stay hydrated, and avoid alcohol at the summit. The excursion takes a full morning, so an early 08:00 departure is recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest day from skiing — lace up snowshoes for a guided family snowshoeing and winter hiking experience in the Grindelwald area (a variation of the Zermatt snowshoeing experience adapted locally). Join a guided snowshoe tour departing from Grindelwald village into the pristine Bachsee or Pfingstegg area. Trek through snow-laden pine forests with stunning Wetterhorn and Eiger backdrops. Suitable for all ages — guides provide snowshoes and poles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the village by midday. In the afternoon, head to the Grindelwald Sports Center or nearby slope for a family-friendly activity: try the snow tubing or sledging area near Bort. Alternatively, visit the Grindelwald ice rink for a fun family skating session (skate rental available on-site, ~CHF 10–15 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Grindelwald. Browse the village boutiques and chocolate shops before dinner. Consider picking up a Swiss Army knife or handmade wood carving as a keepsake.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy at a leisurely pace before the snowshoe tour.
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant Bort (accessible by gondola or on foot) — enjoy a warming bowl of Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and fresh bread with mountain views (~CHF 18–22 per person).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Pizzeria Alpenblick in Grindelwald — wood-fired pizzas, pasta, and salads in a relaxed family-friendly atmosphere (~CHF 22–32 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe tours can be booked through the Grindelwald tourist office or your hotel concierge — half-day guided tours typically cost CHF 35–50 per adult, with reduced rates for children. This is an ideal active recovery day that gives leg muscles a break from skiing while still enjoying the winter landscape. Layers are essential as snowshoeing generates body heat but rest stops can get cold quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes for a second full skiing day — this time explore the Wengen sector. Take the Wengernalp Railway from Grindelwald to Wengen (a car-free village) for a change of scenery. Ski the classic Lauberhorn runs (site of the famous World Cup downhill race) and the sunny Männlichen plateau. The runs here tend to be less crowded than Grindelwald First on a mid-week morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing in the Wengen-Männlichen area through the early afternoon. Take the Männlichen gondola to the summit for a short, flat 'Royal Walk' ridge hike (30 min round trip, no snowshoes needed on packed trail) with 360° Alpine panoramas — perfect for a mid-ski-day photo stop. Ski back down to Wengen and take the train back to Grindelwald by 15:30.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at a Grindelwald bar or hotel lounge — enjoy a Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot chocolate by the fire. Then head out for a special family dinner to celebrate the penultimate evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — aim for an early start to catch the first Wengernalp Railway (~08:00 departure).
meals.lunch: Restaurant Männlichen at the gondola summit — panoramic terrace dining with rösti, sausages, and hot drinks (~CHF 22–28 per person). Sit outside on sunny days for an unforgettable Alpine lunch experience.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter or Hotel Kirchbühl restaurant in Grindelwald — grilled meats, seasonal Swiss specials, and a good local wine selection (~CHF 35–45 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Wengernalp Railway is included with the Jungfrau Travel Pass. Wengen is a car-free village — a wonderful, peaceful contrast to busier resort areas. The Männlichen Royal Walk is one of the most photographed winter walks in Switzerland — bring your camera. Check evening snow forecasts; fresh overnight snowfall would make Day 6 tobogganing even more exciting.

day_by_day.morning: Adventure day! Take an early train or drive toward the Fläsch-Maienfeld area for the Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run — one of Switzerland's most thrilling family toboggan runs stretching over 3km. The journey from Grindelwald takes approximately 2 hours via train (Interlaken → Sargans → Maienfeld), so depart by 08:00. Arrive by 10:00 and spend the morning flying down the run multiple times — sleds available for rental at the top station.
day_by_day.afternoon: After tobogganing, explore the charming wine village of Maienfeld — famously the setting of Johanna Spyri's 'Heidi' novel. Visit the Heidihaus (Heidi's House museum, ~CHF 5 per person) and walk through the picturesque village. Enjoy the contrast of this lower-altitude Rhine Valley landscape before the return train journey to Grindelwald, arriving back by approximately 17:30.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Grindelwald — celebrate with a special dinner. Pack bags partially tonight to ease tomorrow morning's departure.

meals.breakfast: Quick hotel breakfast or packed breakfast to go — early departure required.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Maienfeld village — Restaurant Zum Weissen Kreuz or a local café serving regional Graubünden specialties like Capuns (chard-wrapped pasta rolls) and local wine (~CHF 25–35 per person).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant Glacier in Grindelwald — splurge slightly on a three-course meal with local venison, seasonal vegetables, and a Swiss wine to mark the final night (~CHF 45–60 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch-Maienfeld toboggan run is a full-day excursion — plan the logistics carefully using the SBB app for real-time train schedules. The run is typically open from December through March depending on snow conditions; call ahead (+41 81 302 58 58) or check online to confirm operation. Helmets are recommended for children and available to rent. This is a beloved family highlight that combines thrills with Swiss cultural charm.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — wake up early for one last look at the Eiger from your hotel window. After breakfast, take a gentle farewell walk through Grindelwald village or up to the Dorfstrasse viewpoint for final photos. Check out of the boutique hotel by 11:00. If time allows before departure, stop at the Grindelwald Bakery for fresh Gipfeli (Swiss croissants) and a coffee to go.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the train from Grindelwald back to Zurich Airport (approximately 2.5 hrs via Interlaken Ost). Allow ample time for check-in and security — aim to arrive at Zurich Airport at least 2.5 hours before your departure flight. Browse the excellent duty-free shops at Zurich Airport for last-minute Swiss chocolate (Lindt, Läderach), cheese, or watches.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Zurich Airport. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, mountain adventures, family memories, and Swiss culinary delights as you board your flight home.

meals.breakfast: Final full hotel breakfast — savor the Swiss cheese, fresh bread, and mountain views one last time.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the train or at Interlaken Ost station — Coop to Go or a station café for a quick, affordable bite (~CHF 10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich Airport — Marché restaurant or similar for a final Swiss meal, or save appetite for in-flight service.

day_by_day.notes: Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) trains from Grindelwald to Zurich Airport run reliably every hour — book seats in advance for Sunday travel as trains can be busy with returning weekend visitors. Leave Grindelwald no later than 12:30 for a typical early evening international departure. Return ski rentals and any hired equipment by 10:00 on checkout day. Keep CHF 50–100 in cash for any last-minute tips, small purchases, or incidentals not covered by card.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

With over 200km of marked runs suitable for all skill levels, families can enjoy beginner-friendly blue runs while more experienced skiers tackle challenging red and black descents. Ski school options are available for children aged 3 and up.

experiences.name: Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking in Zermatt
experiences.description: Explore the stunning snow-covered trails around Zermatt on a guided family snowshoeing tour. Trek through pristine alpine forests and open meadows with breathtaking views of the iconic Matterhorn. Guides provide all equipment and tailor the pace for families with children, making it an accessible and memorable winter adventure.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, stretching over 3km through scenic alpine terrain. Rent sleds at the top and race down the illuminated track as a family. Evening runs under the stars add a magical touch, and the nearby village offers warm Swiss hot chocolate and raclette to round off the adventure.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. Enjoy classic cheese fondue made with Gruyère and Emmental, paired with crusty bread, charcuterie, and local Valais wine for adults. Many chalets offer family-friendly menus and a rustic, authentic alpine atmosphere that kids love.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Excursion
experiences.description: Take the iconic cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, walk on the glacier, and enjoy panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The visitor center offers interactive exhibits about alpine science and history, making it both educational and awe-inspiring for the whole family.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00, no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, a pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) whisks the family from the airport directly to the boutique stay in Grindelwald-Wengen, Jungfrau Region (approx. 2–2.5 hours). Enjoy the scenic alpine drive through Interlaken and into the Jungfrau valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in at the boutique property (estimated arrival ~15:30). After settling in, take a leisurely orientation stroll through Grindelwald village — admire the iconic Eiger North Face backdrop, browse the alpine shops, and pick up any last-minute ski essentials. Visit the local ski rental boutique (e.g., Intersport Grindelwald) to get properly fitted for premium ski equipment for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the hotel's in-house restaurant or a short walk to a top-rated local restaurant. Relax, unwind, and toast the start of the alpine adventure with a glass of Swiss Chasselas white wine.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal prior to arrival
meals.lunch: Light snack or meal at Zurich Airport or during the private transfer (pre-order a luxury picnic hamper through the hotel concierge)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte, Grindelwald — a beloved alpine restaurant serving refined Swiss classics including raclette, rösti, and Bernese-style dishes in a warm chalet atmosphere. Reserve a private table by the fire.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer before departure. Ask the hotel concierge to pre-book ski rental fittings and lift passes for Day 2 to avoid morning queues. Confirm all week's activity reservations upon check-in. Pack light layers for the evening stroll as temperatures in Grindelwald in February typically range from -5°C to +3°C.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes — Begin the first full ski day on the world-class Grindelwald-First or Männlichen sectors. With 213km of prepared pistes across Grindelwald, Wengen, and Mürren, there is terrain for every level. Book a private certified ski instructor through the Swiss Ski School for personalized family coaching — perfect for building confidence and technique from day one. Start on the well-groomed blue and red runs above Grindelwald.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing — take the Gondelbahn Grindelwald-Männlichen cable car for breathtaking panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Enjoy the famous 'Royal Walk' ridge traverse before descending the long, sweeping runs back toward Wengen. Intermediate and advanced family members can explore the red and black runs off Lauberhorn — home of the world's longest downhill race course.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a hot shower and spa session (if available). Head out for a premium dinner at one of Grindelwald's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss alpine breakfast at the boutique hotel — freshly baked bread, local cheeses, cold cuts, bircher muesli, fresh fruit, and hot beverages
meals.lunch: On-mountain lunch at Bergrestaurant Grindelwald-First — enjoy panoramic terrace dining with hearty alpine fare including mountain soup, club sandwiches, and warm Apfelstrudel with vanilla sauce
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter, Grindelwald — known for premium grilled meats and creative alpine cuisine. Order the dry-aged Swiss beef or the truffle risotto, paired with a bottle of Pinot Noir from Graubünden

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Jungfrau VIP Ski Pass (Top Ski Pass) for the full week to access all lifts across the region seamlessly. Private ski lessons should be booked 48 hours in advance. Dress in high-performance ski layers — base layer, mid-layer fleece, and a waterproof shell jacket. Apply high-SPF sunscreen as UV exposure at altitude is intense even on cloudy days.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Excursion — Take the iconic cogwheel train from Grindelwald Grund or Kleine Scheidegg up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters — the highest railway station in Europe. Depart early (around 08:00) to beat the crowds and enjoy the clearest morning views. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, the longest glacier in the Alps, from the Sphinx Observatory viewing terrace. Explore the Ice Palace, carved entirely within the glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — try the snow activities on the plateau including short snowshoe walks, snow disc rides, and husky sled photo opportunities (seasonal). Visit the Alpine Sensation exhibition inside the mountain. Begin the scenic descent back by early afternoon, arriving in Grindelwald by approximately 14:30–15:00. Spend the remaining afternoon at leisure — visit the Grindelwald Sports Centre or enjoy a family ice skating session at the local rink.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening — spa and wellness at the hotel followed by a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast (request 07:00 service from the hotel) — continental spread with Swiss pastries, yogurt, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Aletsch Restaurant or Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch (3,454m) — a truly once-in-a-lifetime dining experience above the clouds. Enjoy a warm three-course set menu with panoramic glacier views
meals.dinner: Chalet Hotel Bellevue des Alpes, Kleine Scheidegg (or equivalent in Grindelwald) — an elegant historic mountain hotel restaurant serving classic French-Swiss cuisine. Try the fondue bourguignonne or the pan-seared Alpine trout

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead in peak February season. Dress in extra warm layers for Jungfraujoch as temperatures at the summit can reach -15°C to -20°C with wind chill. Children and adults may experience mild altitude effects — take it slowly and stay hydrated. Bring sunglasses with UV400 protection. The excursion from Grindelwald and back takes approximately 5–6 hours total.

day_by_day.morning: Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking in the Jungfrau Region — Rather than traveling to Zermatt (a 3-hour journey), arrange a premium guided family snowshoeing experience locally in the Grindelwald-First area or around the Bachalpsee lake trail. A certified mountain guide leads the family through pristine snow-covered forests and open alpine meadows, with stunning views of the Wetterhorn and Schreckhorn peaks. The Bachalpsee trail (approx. 6km round trip) is manageable for families and extraordinarily scenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the snowshoe tour (approx. 13:00), enjoy a relaxed afternoon at the hotel spa. Many boutique alpine properties offer heated pools, saunas, steam rooms, and massage treatments — book a family-friendly après-ski massage or a couple's hot stone treatment. Alternatively, explore the Grindelwald village on foot, visiting local artisan chocolate shops and Swiss watch boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience — Warm up with a traditional Swiss fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. This quintessential Swiss experience features classic cheese fondue (Gruyère and Emmental), fondue chinoise, and raclette, served with alpine breads, potatoes, and pickles.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — hot options including scrambled eggs, bacon, and smoked salmon alongside the classic Swiss spread
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the hotel — a premium packed lunch delivered to the snowshoe trail midpoint, featuring artisan sandwiches, Swiss chocolate, thermos of hot soup, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte or Berghaus Bort, Grindelwald — an authentic Swiss chalet fondue experience with roaring fireplace, cowbell décor, and live accordion music. Pair with a bottle of Fendant (Swiss Chasselas) from Valais

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe rentals and poles can be arranged through the hotel concierge or at Grindelwald-First gondola station. The guided snowshoe tour should be pre-booked through a local guide company such as Grindelwald Sports or Bergführerbüro Grindelwald. Wear waterproof hiking boots or ski boots — snowshoes attach over any footwear. The fondue dinner reservation should be made 2–3 days in advance as these intimate chalet restaurants fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Full Day Skiing — Wengen Sector Exploration. Today, take the train from Grindelwald to Wengen (the car-free village) and explore the Lauberhorn and Männlichen ski areas from the Wengen side. Wengen offers beautifully wide, groomed runs perfect for family skiing. The Lauberhorn World Cup Downhill course is one of the most iconic in ski racing history — advanced skiers can attempt sections of it. Book a second private ski lesson or guided freeride session for the family to explore off-piste powder areas safely.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tobogganing on a Local Run — After lunch, enjoy a thrilling family tobogganing session. The Grindelwald-First toboggan run (2km) is a fantastic family activity accessible directly from the First gondola. Alternatively, the Männlichen toboggan run offers spectacular scenery. Rent premium wooden or plastic toboggans at the top station and race down the prepared track — an unforgettable family memory.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory mid-trip dinner at the finest restaurant in the region.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a packed breakfast bag if departing early for the Wengen train
meals.lunch: Restaurant Jungfrau, Wengen — an elegant mountain restaurant with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the Jungfrau massif. Enjoy a leisurely three-course lunch with fresh alpine salad, mushroom risotto, and warm chocolate fondant
meals.dinner: Restaurant Français at the Grand Hotel Regina or equivalent fine dining in Grindelwald — white tablecloth dining featuring seasonal tasting menus with wine pairing. Expect dishes like venison with juniper berry jus, truffle pasta, and a Swiss cheese trolley

day_by_day.notes: The Grindelwald–Wengen train runs frequently (every 30 minutes) and is included with the regional transport pass. Tobogganing is suitable for children aged 5 and above — younger children can ride with an adult. Helmets are recommended and usually available for rental at the top station. Book the fine dining dinner at least 3–4 days in advance and note any dietary requirements.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing — Mürren and Schilthorn Sector. Take the scenic route to Mürren — the dramatic car-free cliff-top village — via Lauterbrunnen and the cable car. Ski the Schilthorn area (2,970m), famous as the filming location for the James Bond film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service.' The Inferno run from Schilthorn to Lauterbrunnen (15.8km) is one of the longest ski descents in the Alps — suitable for confident intermediate to advanced skiers. Younger or beginner family members can enjoy the gentler slopes around Mürren village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Piz Gloria revolving restaurant at the top of Schilthorn for a James Bond-themed experience — browse the 007 exhibition and enjoy the 360-degree panoramic views of 200 Alpine peaks including the Eiger, Mönch, Jungfrau, and Matterhorn on clear days. Return to Grindelwald by mid-afternoon. Spend the final free afternoon at the hotel — enjoy the spa, pack souvenirs, or take a final peaceful walk through the village.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell family dinner — celebrate the end of an extraordinary alpine week.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — indulge in the complete spread including hot dishes, pastries, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Piz Gloria Revolving Restaurant, Schilthorn Summit (2,970m) — a truly iconic dining experience. Enjoy the James Bond-themed menu with panoramic 360-degree views. Try the 'Blofeld Platter' or classic Swiss dishes with a dramatic alpine backdrop
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant Adler or a private chalet dinner arranged by the hotel concierge — a fully catered private fondue and raclette feast in a rented chalet, complete with a fondue master, Swiss wine selection, and traditional Swiss desserts including Meringues with double cream

day_by_day.notes: The journey to Mürren requires the Lauterbrunnen valley train and cable car — allow 1.5 hours from Grindelwald. The Schilthorn cable car ticket is not included in the standard Jungfrau Ski Pass and requires a separate supplement. Book the private chalet dinner farewell experience through the hotel concierge at least 3 days in advance. This is an exceptional and highly memorable way to end the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in the Alps — Wake up early for one last sunrise over the Eiger from the hotel terrace or balcony — a moment of pure alpine magic. Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at the hotel. Take a short morning walk through Grindelwald village to pick up last-minute Swiss souvenirs: Lindt or Läderach chocolates, Swiss Army knives, local cheese, or a bottle of Swiss Kirsch. If time permits, take a final gondola ride up to Grindelwald-First for one last panoramic view of the Jungfrau region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique hotel (standard check-out 11:00 — request a late check-out until 12:00 or 13:00 if the flight schedule permits). The pre-arranged private luxury transfer departs for the airport (Zurich or Geneva depending on return flight). Enjoy the scenic alpine drive one final time, passing through Interlaken and along the shores of Lake Brienz or Lake Thun.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — airport arrival, check-in, and homeward bound with extraordinary Swiss alpine memories.

meals.breakfast: Final grand hotel breakfast — a slow, celebratory morning meal. Request a special Swiss breakfast spread including regional specialties: Berner Platte cold cuts, Emmental cheese, Zopf braided bread, and hot chocolate
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at Café Bar 3692 or Bäckerei Grindelwald in the village before departure — artisan sandwiches, Swiss pastries, and a final coffee with a view of the Eiger
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight — ask the hotel to arrange a premium airport lounge access (e.g., Swiss Senator Lounge at Zurich Airport) for a comfortable pre-flight meal and drinks

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transfer departure time to allow at least 3–3.5 hours before the flight (Grindelwald to Zurich Airport is approximately 2–2.5 hours). Return all ski rental equipment to the shop the evening before or first thing in the morning. Confirm luggage storage at the hotel if checking out before the transfer departs. Consider shipping any excess luggage directly to the airport via the Swiss Fly Luggage (Fly Gepäck) service — luggage is collected from the hotel and delivered to the airport check-in, allowing hands-free travel.
